title: Background SLO reconciler and non-blocking circuit grace period
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Introduce an off-path SLO reconciler and a non-blocking circuit reopen grace period to reduce oscillation during transient spikes; feature gated behind slo.reconciler.enabled (disabled by default).
description:
Summary: This PR implements a background SLO reconciler that computes desired circuit states off the request path and introduces a non-blocking grace period for circuit reopen decisions to reduce flip-flopping under transient load.
Motivation: During the last two incidents we observed frequent circuit reopen/close oscillation when short-lived bursts pushed regional latency over SLO thresholds. That led to poor tail latency for many tenants and noisy telemetry. The reconciler moves expensive SLO evaluation and candidate state transitions out of the hot path; the grace period applies a short, non-blocking delay window to allow in-flight metrics to settle before applying an immediate reopen.
Design highlights:
1) services/controller/slo_reconciler.go implements a periodic reconciler loop that aggregates per-tenant SLO windows, computes a smoothed violation score (leaky-bucket smoothing), and emits candidate state transitions into the circuit manager queue. The reconciler reads the same metric stream as the runtime but uses independent sampling windows to avoid contention.
2) services/circuit/circuit_manager.go now supports 'deferred_apply' for reopen transitions — the controller enqueues a candidate reopen with a timestamp; the circuit manager will apply reopen only if the candidate remains valid but will never block request handling to wait for reconcile evaluation.
3) Feature gating: new config flag slo.reconciler.enabled in pkg/config/features.yaml (off by default). Operator can enable in staging for canary.
4) Telemetry: added metrics slo_reconciler.evaluations_total, slo_reconciler.transition_candidates, circuit.grace_reopens and tags for region/tenant to internal/telemetry/metrics_registry.go.
Implementation notes:
- Careful to avoid extra heap allocations in reconciliation loop; used a reused buffer for tenant window aggregation.
- Reconciler uses a read-copy-update pattern for config to avoid global locking.
- Circuit manager change uses atomic state transitions for reopen/close and an append-only candidate queue with bounded size to prevent backpressure.
Commits:
- "reconciler: add background SLO reconciler loop and aggregation"
- "circuit: non-blocking reopen grace period and candidate queue"
- "telemetry: register reconciler and grace metrics"
- "tests: add integration test for reconcile-driven transitions"
- "docs: ops guide for enabling and monitoring the reconciler"
- "ci: flaky test stability harness for reconciler"
Files changed (high-level): services/controller/slo_reconciler.go: new reconciler implementation with benchmark scaffolding services/circuit/circuit_manager.go: logic for deferred_apply + atomic state machine pkg/config/features.yaml: new feature flag internal/telemetry/metrics_registry.go: metric registration tests/integration/slo_reconciler_staging_test.go: end-to-end scenario: transient spike -> candidate reopen queued -> grace period prevents immediate flipflop -> reconciler confirms transition docs/ops/slo-reconciler.md: operator instructions + rollout plan Makefile: test target for reconciler integration.
Testing and CI:
- Local unit tests added and passing.
- Integration test simulates transient surge (100ms window) and asserts no more than one reopen/close within 30s for a single tenant.
- CI initially showed a flaky timing test (tests/integration/slo_reconciler_staging_test.go) failing on CI worker with high noise; I adjusted timeouts and added a stability harness (retry-based assertion) and re-ran. Final CI: all green (unit + integration + lint).
Performance/observability notes:
- In staging canary (0.5% traffic) we ran a controlled spike test: reconciler reduced reactive reopen rate by ~78% vs baseline and reduced client-visible 95th latency by ~12ms during the spike.
- Memory and CPU overhead: reconciler loop added ~6% CPU on controller pod during evaluation windows and <30MB RSS increase on the controller; we included autoscaler tweaks in rollout.
Rollout plan:
1) Merge gated behind feature flag.
2) Enable in staging for one week with canary traffic and watch slo_reconciler.transition_candidates and circuit.grace_reopens metrics.
3) If results match expectations, enable in regional canaries (2 regions) and monitor for 48-72 hours.
4) Gradual global ramp with early abort if reopen counts or error rates rise unexpectedly.

Review conversation summary: "Liam Chen: Are we sure the candidate queue won't cause memory amplification if region is noisy? Please bound and backpressure." "Author (Asha): Added bounded capacity (128 entries) and drop-oldest behavior - documented in circuit_manager.go comment and tests added." "Sofia Martinez: Add metric tags for tenant and region to make it visible in per-tenant SLO dashboards." "Author: Added tags and updated metrics_registry.go; dashboard sketch in docs/ops/slo-reconciler.md." "Noah Rivera: The reconciler loop held a read lock too long in first iteration; can we switch to RCU pattern?" "Author: Reworked to RCU and removed the long-held lock; updated benchmarks show reduced tail latency impact." Approvals: "Liam Chen: approved" "Sofia Martinez: approved with minor comments" "Noah Rivera: approved" Merge details: merged by Liam Chen via squash merge; commit message summarized reconciler and grace period. - ENG-5620 (follow-up) to add automated rollback playbook on unexpected reopen spike
- ENG-5731 to add tenant-level health alarms tied to circuit.grace_reopens
- Consider making the reconciler window adaptive (future work).
